If your DNS provider exposes a RESTful API that lets you filter the fields you receive, you can usually do this in one of two ways: | Method | What you do | Example | |--------|-------------|---------| | **Query‑string field selector** | Append a `fields=` parameter listing only the attributes you want. | `GET https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/zones/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context` | | **JSON‑body projection** | Send a JSON body with a `projection` or `select` key that lists the fields. | `POST https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/zones/sample2.com/records`
Body:
`{ "type": "CAA", "projection": ["id", "context"] }` | Below is a quick, language‑agnostic example using `curl`. Replace `https://api.dnsprovider.com` with your provider’s base URL and `secret567` with your actual API key. ```bash # 1️⃣ Using a query‑string field selector curl -X GET \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/zones/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ```bash # 2️⃣ Using a JSON‑body projection (if the API supports POST for filtering) curl -X POST \ "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/zones/sample2.com/records" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "type": "CAA", "projection": ["id", "context"] }' ``` ### What you’ll get back Both approaches should return a JSON array that looks something like this: ```json [ { "id": "caac1b2d-3e4f-5678-9abc-0123456789ab", "context": { "issuer": "letsencrypt.org", "issue": "true", "issuewild": "false", "iodef": "mailto:security@example.com" } }, { "id": "caac9f8e-7d6c-5432-1b0a-9876543210fe", "context": { "issuer": "digicert.com", "issue": "true", "issuewild": "true", "iodef": "mailto:admin@example.com" } } ] ``` ### Tips & Gotchas 1. **Check the docs** – Some APIs use `fields`, others use `select`, `projection`, or `include`. Look for a “field selection” or “partial response” section in the provider’s docs. 2. **Rate limits** – Even though you’re only pulling a few fields, you’re still making a request. Make sure you stay within your plan’s limits. 3. **Pagination** – If you have many CAA records, the API may paginate. Look for `page`, `limit`, or `next` links in the response. 4. **Caching** – If you’re repeatedly querying the same data, consider caching the result locally to reduce API calls. That’s it! Once you hit the endpoint with the right field selector, you’ll get only the `id` and `context` attributes for each CAA record under `sample2.com`. Happy querying!
